sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Non-permeabilizing confocal immunofluorescence confirmed plasma membrane localisation of both wild-type and Arg394His KCNH7 constructs carrying the tag; channel electrophysiology was not separately reported for the tagged construct in this study.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the V5 tag was inserted between amino acids 441 and 442 of the S1-S2 extracellular loop of full-length KCNH7. Python verification confirms position 441 (R) and 442 (R) both fall within the authoritative extracellular span 433-452, 9 residues from the TM1 C-terminus (432) and 12 residues from the TM2 N-terminus (453), both well above the ≥3 aa minimum. Two downstream cysteines (444, 448) are present in the loop but are C-terminal to the insert junction, and the paper demonstrates successful surface trafficking, indicating the tag does not disrupt folding or membrane targeting. Full-length KCNH7 (Kv11.3/ERG3) carrying a V5 epitope tag (GKPIPNPLLGLDST, 14 aa) inserted between residues 441 and 442 in the S1-S2 extracellular loop was expressed in Neuro-2a cells; surface display was assessed by indirect immunofluorescence under non-permeabilizing conditions.

sources.claim: To assess membrane localization of KCNH7 subunits, the V5 epitope tag (GKPIPNPLLGLDST) was inserted between amino acids 441 and 442 of the S1-S2 extracellular loop of KCNH7 and indirect immunofluorescence labeling was performed under non-permeabilizing conditions.

literature_notes: Two ledger lines (L1 and L2) both derive from PMC4222358 and describe the same V5 insertion at the 441|442 junction; L1 is the primary citation as it contains the explicit residue statement and tag sequence. No other extracellular insertion sites are supported by the ledger. The S3-S4 loop (513-519, only 7 residues) and the S5-S6 pore loop (571-641) are extracellular but no ledger line reports a tolerated insertion in those regions for KCNH7 or a close ortholog. The large intracellular N-terminus (1-411) and C-terminus (663-1196) are not surface-accessible and were not considered. Cysteines at 444 and 448 in the S1-S2 loop are noted; they lie downstream of the 441|442 junction and the paper's positive surface-trafficking result demonstrates they are compatible with the insert.
